newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ATAN favours Markermeer option for Dutch airport.
newsitem.headline: ATAN favours Markermeer option for Dutch airport.

text.p: ATAN, the Dutch Air Transport Association, said it favours the option of building a new Dutch airport on a specially-built polder in the Markermeer lake.

In a report in cooperation with Amkreutz Airport Consultants, ATAN found in favour of the option of the airport in Markermeer lake as opposed to plans to develop a new Dutch airport in the North Sea or on the Maasvlakte in Rotterdam.
As Amsterdam Schiphol Airport nears full capacity, three options are being considered for the future of Dutch aviation.
Under the Maasvlakte option, the development of a second airport on Rotterdam's Maasvlakte would be used for charter and cargo carriers.

However, the possibility of developing a second land reclamation project at the Maasvlakte has also not yet got the go-ahead. A reclamation area of up to 1,000 hectares is currently being considered by the government.
Another airport option favours building an island in the North Sea around ten kilometres off the Dutch coast.
ATAN spokesman Hans Knuvers said the organisation is very much in favour of making optimal use of Schiphol's capacity before any other airport is built.
"Schiphol's capacity should not be limited because of political considerations but realistic ones," he stressed.
ATAN believes that Schiphol could be used beyond the 44 million passenger and 3.3 million tonnes of cargo which are the government recommended caps for the Dutch airport, he said.
At the current 12 percent growth rate, Schiphol will reach this limit by the year 2003.
It is only after Schiphol is utilised to its full capacity that a second airport should be developed, he added.
In the report, considerations such as possible 24-hour operation, capacity levels, noise and environmental constraints were all looked into.
A decision on the second airport also needs to be taken very soon as it will probably take at least ten years to develop, Knuvers said.
ATAN considers the North Sea option too costly and too risky because connection to the mainland would be very expensive.
Markermeer would be a cheaper option and the polder offers enough cheap space for distribution companies.
The study argues that the Maasvlakte would also be expensive as connections between Rotterdam port and Schiphol would be too costly. Expansion possibilities are also limited.
ATAN also does not believe that freight and passenger flights should be separated which is the case under the Maasvlakte option.
On June 10, Amsterdam Schiphol Airport's president Hans Smits said Schiphol airport prefered the North Sea island option.
